title: The Contractor Nobody Checks
briefing: Priya Okafor has a follow-up from Northgate. Kelvarin Refrigeration Services maintains the compressors at all six Valtren sites, and the contract renews automatically in ten weeks.
Tomasz Brennan, Head of Procurement, wants a risk view before he lets it roll over. Review the file and recommend what Valtren should do.

context.text: Since R-014 was accepted without action, Priya wants this one done properly: "Show me the evidence, not the contract."
The Northgate repair you recommended was carried out by Kelvarin. Operations want to know whether they can rely on the contractor for the other sites.
Procurement is wary of the risk team after recent events. Expect your recommendation to be challenged.

evidence.title: Maintenance contract - service levels (extract)
body: Kelvarin will service every compressor quarterly and respond to breakdowns within 4 hours, 24/7.
Service visits are recorded by Kelvarin's engineer in the site service log. Kelvarin certifies completion in its monthly invoice.
Term: 24 months, renewing automatically for 12 months unless either party gives 60 days' notice. No service credits.

evidence.title: Service log summary, last four quarters
body: Northgate: Q1 done, Q2 not recorded, Q3 done, Q4 not recorded.
Eastfield: Q1 done, Q2 done, Q3 not recorded, Q4 done.
Every entry is signed by a Kelvarin engineer. No Valtren signature or check appears on any visit. All four quarters were invoiced as complete.

evidence.title: Supplier questionnaire (self-assessment)
body: Kelvarin rates itself 'fully compliant' on safety, quality and continuity.
Attached F-gas handling certificate expired eight months ago. No business continuity plan was provided ('available on request').

evidence.title: Procurement note
body: Kelvarin is the only approved refrigeration contractor for all six sites. Spend last year: 410,000.
Switching would take about four months including site surveys. Procurement has had no complaint logged against Kelvarin.

evidence.title: Email from Priya Okafor
evidence.body: Keep it practical. Tomasz needs a recommendation he can act on before the notice date, not a lecture on third-party risk.

questions.prompt: Which of these are genuine risks from the Kelvarin arrangement, based on the evidence?

options.label: One contractor maintains every site, so a Kelvarin failure hits all six at once
Missed services go unnoticed because Kelvarin records and certifies its own visits
Refrigerant handling by staff whose certification has lapsed
Automatic renewal locks Valtren into terms with no service credits
Diesel price rises increase Kelvarin's call-out charges
options.feedback: Nothing in the file links Kelvarin's charges to fuel prices: that is speculation, not a risk from the evidence.

options.label: Procurement has logged no complaints, so the relationship is low risk
options.feedback: No complaints is not evidence of good service: nobody at Valtren checks the visits.

questions.prompt: How would you rate the residual risk that Kelvarin fails to maintain the compressors (5x5 matrix)?

options.label: Likelihood 4, impact 4 (High): two sites already missed services and every site depends on Kelvarin
options.feedback: Missed visits at two sites in a year make failure likely; the impact spans all six sites.

options.label: Likelihood 2, impact 4: the contract requires quarterly servicing
options.feedback: A contract clause is not a control that operates: the log shows it is not being met.

options.label: Likelihood 4, impact 2: a late service is an inconvenience
options.feedback: Northgate showed what a missed service can lead to: spoiled stock and client penalties.

options.label: Likelihood 5, impact 5 (Critical): stop using Kelvarin today
options.feedback: The evidence supports High, not certain catastrophe; stopping today would leave every site without cover.

questions.prompt: How effective is the current control: 'Kelvarin records each visit in the service log and certifies completion on its invoice'?

options.label: Ineffective: the same party performs and checks the work, and nobody at Valtren reconciles visits to invoices
options.feedback: Right: there is no independent check, and invoices for missed quarters were paid.

options.label: Partially effective: a log exists, so gaps can be found
options.feedback: Gaps can be found only if someone looks. Nobody does, so the log detects nothing.

options.label: Effective: the contract requires the log and the invoice certification
options.feedback: A requirement on paper is not an operating control.

questions.prompt: What do you recommend to Procurement before the notice date? Your approval authority is shown at the top of the screen.

options.label: Let it renew; raise performance at the next quarterly meeting
options.feedback: This leaves unverified servicing in place for another year at every site.

schedules.description: Unserviced compressor fails at Eastfield during a delivery peak

options.label: Renew for 12 months only with service credits, Valtren site sign-off for every visit, a current certificate within 30 days, and a second approved contractor by Q3
options.feedback: Keeps cover in place while fixing the control (independent sign-off) and the concentration (second contractor).

options.label: Terminate Kelvarin and move all sites to a new contractor now (60,000 transition cost)
options.feedback: Switching all six sites in a hurry creates its own gap in cover, and it is not your spend to approve.

schedules.description: No contractor on call at two sites during the changeover

options.label: Escalate a business case to exit Kelvarin to the Head of Procurement, with interim site sign-off of visits
options.feedback: Escalating is right for a decision above your authority, but exit is a bigger step than the evidence needs while conditions could fix it.

questions.prompt: How do you put this to Tomasz Brennan?

options.label: Lead with the decision and the deadline (notice in 10 weeks), the evidence (missed quarters paid as complete), the recommended conditions and who owns them
options.feedback: Decision, deadline, evidence, owner: everything he needs to act.

options.label: Send the full questionnaire analysis and let him draw conclusions
options.feedback: Detail without a recommendation pushes the work back to him.

options.label: Mark the risk red in the register and wait for Procurement to ask
options.feedback: A colour in a register nobody reads before the notice date changes nothing.

options.label: Email the CEO directly so it gets attention
options.feedback: Bypassing the accountable owner damages trust and skips the people who can fix it.

lesson: A control performed and checked by the same party is not a control. Third-party risk needs independent evidence, and contract dates are risk dates.
